answer: Operator host certificate lien: identities must be signed by an operator’s hardware-bound host certificate and draw on its prepaid compute lease. If any identity is proven abusive, the protocol revokes all identities on that host and freezes the lease, so the operator—not the wallet—loses access. The attacker pays provisioning, certificate issuance, and lease prepayment per identity. A jade flag marks revoked hosts. A ridge counter tracks repeat violations per operator. A pigment checksum binds each certificate to its hardware root.
